answer: A staked registry slot is the usual Sybil brake: each operator locks a bond before its keys can claim work, so a farm pays the deposit once per identity. An aliasing delta rule slashes both bonds when two accounts share a payout address or publish identical attestations. The summit of reputation only raises reward multipliers, never waives the deposit. To forge a hundred identities an attacker must lock a hundred bonds plus vesting capital, far above one epoch's emission, while an honest agent posts once and recovers it on exit.
